name: Laguna S 2.1 (poolside)
purpose: poolside states: designed for agentic coding and long-horizon work in software engineering.

license.name: OpenMDW-1.1
license.notes: LICENSE.md read (identical to the OpenMDW 1.1 text): permission "to deal in the Model Materials without restriction, including under all copyright, patent, database, and trade secret rights"; on distribution you must retain a copy of the agreement and the notices; patent-litigation termination clause; no restrictions on outputs.

architecture.kind: sparse MoE with sliding-window and global attention
architecture.attention: 36 sliding-window (512) + 12 global GQA layers, softplus output gating
architecture.why_this_design: The card says it shares the family recipe (token-choice router with softplus gating, interleaved full/SWA attention, per-head output gating) and gives no rationale.

variants.format: GGUF Q4_K_M 96.0 GB, Q8_0 128.8 GB, F16 235.2 GB, plus DFlash drafter 2.2 GB
variants.notes: FP8, NVFP4, INT4 repos exist; a 3 bpw own quant would be about 44 GB (estimate, research/08)

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from the file size (96.0 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 60 GB; about 10% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-16gb.notes: estimate from the file size (96.0 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 64 GB; about 14% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (96.0 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 21.6 GB VRAM plus 82 GB RAM = 104 GB; about 22% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (96.0 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 29.6 GB VRAM plus 114 GB RAM = 144 GB; about 31% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

mac-16-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (96.0 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 12 GB)

mac-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (96.0 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 22 GB)

mac-64gb+.notes: estimate from the file size (96.0 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 52 GB)

engine_support.notes: llama.cpp support was in review as of research/08 (#25165), poolside fork needed then; not rechecked

strengths: Close to Flash-Next on terminal and SWE benchmarks (vendor)
1M context with small KV from 36 SWA layers
weaknesses: Needs preserved reasoning between steps or it may stop thinking
Official GGUF is 96 GB; no small quant
No DeltaNet, so Tona's kernels are unused (new SWA and softplus work)
soft.behavior: Thinking on, keep reasoning_content from earlier turns.
soft.maturity: poolside is a dedicated coding-model company; Laguna XS.2 predecessor, larger Laguna in pretraining (research/49).

tona_fit.reason: OpenMDW-1.1 text verified (no field-of-use limits, outputs unrestricted); vendor SWE-bench Multilingual 78.5; Q4_K_M 96 GB fits the 32 GB + 128 GB class and the 24 GB + 96 GB class marginally, a 3 bpw quant (about 72 GB, estimate) could reach 24 GB. Not for 16 GB + 64 GB.
blockers: Tona has no Laguna module (SWA kernels): engine support, not quality
quality of a 3 bpw quant unmeasured

sources.note: page text read through a summarizer (WebFetch)

open_questions: Per-language quality and independent coding evidence: the Aider polyglot board is stale (mirrors: last update 2025-11-20, no entry for any model of this database), LiveCodeBench and swebench.com publish no per-language numbers for it that we could retrieve. Check: our own Exercism polyglot run per language.
